answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by licensing one lighthouse lens-polishing season per identity. The keeper climbs one lighthouse, polishes its pearl-white lens, and logs each night's beam in an umber-stamped book, while a raven nesting above marks dawn. Random checks summon the keeper to that lens on camera within hours; one person cannot tend two lighthouses at once. The license fee in outside money doubles per further lighthouse on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another lighthouse, another season of climbs, another human, and twice the prior fee.
